files.purpose: A caseless enum `CommandCodeAPI` that holds every non-session piece of the Command Code (`cmd`) provider: locating the API key (env `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY` first, else `~/.commandcode/auth.json`), reading the CLI's `~/.commandcode/config.json`, probing sign-in with `cmd status --no-auto-update`, and fetching plan windows and dollar credits from `https://api.commandcode.ai/alpha/billing/credits` and `/alpha/billing/subscriptions`. It also parses `cmd --list-models --no-auto-update` output into `ModelOption`s (with display names, per-model reasoning-effort lists and context-window sizes from hard-coded tables that mirror `cmd 1.53.1`), ships a 9-entry seed catalog, and embeds the TypeScript approval mod (`droppy-code-approvals.ts`) that CommandCodeSession loads with `--mod` to gate tool calls through request/reply files and to register MCP tools from the Droppy MCP bridge.

The embedded mod (run by the CLI, not the app), per gated call: unlinks any stale `<id>.reply.json` first (line 410 `try { fs.unlinkSync(reply) } catch {}`), writes `<id>.request.json.tmp` and renames it to `<id>.request.json` (lines 411-412), then polls `<id>.reply.json` every 40 ms. When a reply arrives it unlinks ONLY the reply (line 418) and leaves the request file alone (on the normal path the app deletes the request as it reads it, CommandCodeSession.swift:676 `try? fileManager.removeItem(at: file)`). The mod unlinks the request itself only on abort (line 425) or on `process.ppid === 1` / 6-hour timeout (line 429). Separately, when DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE is set it dynamically imports that file (line 390 `import(bridgePath)`).
platform_assumptions: FileManager `.applicationSupportDirectory` in `.userDomainMask`, fallback `<home>/Library/Application Support` (macOS path); Windows needs %APPDATA%/%LOCALAPPDATA% equivalent.
HOME environment variable and `~/.commandcode/...` paths (Windows uses USERPROFILE).
Shell.run process spawning of the `cmd` executable (on Windows `cmd` collides with cmd.exe naming; the port must resolve the Command Code binary explicitly).
Mod's `process.ppid === 1` orphan check is a POSIX assumption (on Windows the parent pid does not become 1 when the parent dies).
Mod ids sanitised with `/[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]/g` -> '_' keep file names valid on Windows too.

Line 390 `import(bridgePath)` passes the raw value of `process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE`, which CommandCodeSession.swift:175 sets to `bridge.path` (a filesystem path, not a URL). On Windows that is a drive-letter path (`C:\...`); Node's ESM loader rejects a bare absolute Windows path in dynamic `import()` (it needs a `file://` URL, e.g. via `pathToFileURL`), unless the CLI's TypeScript compilation turns `import()` into `require()`, which this file does not define. Any failure is swallowed by line 400 `.catch((error: any) => console.error('droppy mcp', error))`, so the only symptom is that no MCP tools appear. The port must pass a `file://` URL or verify the CLI's loader on Windows.

The registration code runs before the `if (!dir) return` approvals check (lines 402-403), so it runs even when DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS is unset, BUT only when the mod is loaded at all: CommandCodeSession.swift:162-165 passes `--mod` only `if let modURL, runtimeMode != .fullAccess || interactionMode == .plan || FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path)`. files.purpose: The `@MainActor final class CommandCodeSession: ProviderSession` that runs Command Code in headless print mode: every turn spawns a fresh `cmd -p --output-format json ...` StdioProcess with the prompt on stdin, parses newline-delimited `event` frames and a final `result` line into ProviderEvents, and resumes the conversation with `--resume <sessionId>`. It implements Droppy's approval modes by running the CLI with `--yolo` plus the CommandCodeAPI approval mod, watching a per-session approval directory for `<id>.request.json` files, auto-answering by runtime mode and session grants or raising an ApprovalRequest, and writing `<id>.reply.json` back; exit codes and result subtypes are mapped to completion states and actionable error text.

side_effects: start(): installs the mod file, creates `<supportDirectory>/approvals/<UUID().uuidString>/` (lines 104-107), and calls startWatcher, which opens the directory with `open(directory.path, O_EVTONLY)`; `guard descriptor >= 0 else { return }` (lines 652-653) means that if the open fails the session runs with NO watcher and no error or notice. Requests are then picked up only by the `scanApprovals()` call in tool_queued (line 372; the only other caller is the watcher handler, line 656), so a request written after its tool_queued event is never seen and the mod keeps polling until the turn is aborted, the parent pid becomes 1, or 6 hours pass.

send(): spawns the CLI per turn and writes the prompt to stdin then closes it. Environment (lines 168-179), starting from configuration.environment: `if runtimeMode != .fullAccess, let approvalDirectory { environment["DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS"] = approvalDirectory.path } else { environment["DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS"] = nil }`, i.e. in Full access (or with no approval directory) any inherited DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS is actively removed; `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE = bridge.path` whenever `try? MCPBridge.installBridge()` succeeds, regardless of mode; `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG = MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path` when that file exists. DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG is not read by the approval mod; it is read by the bridge script (DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPBridgeSource.swift:21 `const file = process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG || "";`), so it must be kept for MCP tools to find their servers. Consequence: `--mod` is added only when `runtimeMode != .fullAccess || interactionMode == .plan || fileExists(MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path)` (lines 162-165), so in Full access, outside plan mode, with no Claude config file, DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE is set but nothing loads it.
Reads target files up to 1_000_000 bytes as UTF-8 for write_file before/after snapshots.

Deletes request files as it reads them; writes reply files via temp file + FileManager.replaceItemAt (fallback direct atomic write); clears all files in the approval directory when a run closes; removes the whole approval directory on stop().
platform_assumptions: DispatchSourceFileSystemObject with POSIX `open(path, O_EVTONLY)` and eventMask [.write] on the main queue (macOS kqueue); Windows needs FileSystemWatcher / ReadDirectoryChangesW or polling.
SIGTERM semantics and exit status 130 for an interrupted run; Windows process termination yields a different exit code, so interruptRequested is the reliable signal.
FileManager.replaceItemAt for atomic reply swap (Windows: MoveFileEx/ReplaceFile).
Error text tells the user to run `cmd login` "in Terminal" (macOS app name).
Doc comment says a session may belong to "another Mac's" transcript.

The watcher failure path is silent (line 653 `guard descriptor >= 0 else { return }`); a Windows FileSystemWatcher replacement must decide explicitly whether to fail, poll, or run without a watcher (upstream: runs without one).

Ids use Swift `UUID().uuidString`, which is UPPERCASE hex: `launchID = String(UUID().uuidString.prefix(8))` (line 42), giving ids like `cc-E621E1F8-m1`, `cc-E621E1F8-r1`, `cc-E621E1F8-plan1`; the approval directory is named with the full uppercase `UUID().uuidString` (line 106). JS `crypto.randomUUID()` is lowercase, so parity needs `.toUpperCase()`.
persisted_fields: No app persistence here; sessionID reaches the host via .sessionReady(sessionID:) and returns as configuration.resumeID.
Approval request JSON read: `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `input`; file suffix `.request.json`.

Reply JSON written: allow -> {"decision": "allow"}; deny -> {"decision": "deny", "reason": "The user declined this in Droppy Code. Do not retry it; take another approach or explain what you would need."}; file `<id>.reply.json` via `<id>.reply.json.tmp`.
CLI transcripts at `~/.commandcode/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` (read for existence only).
ui_elements: Approval options in order: id "allow" title "Approve" role .approve; id "always" title "Approve for session" role .approveAlways; id "deny" title "Decline" role .decline. ApprovalRequest title/detail come from makeToolCall; toolItemID set only when the tool row exists.

Tool rows from makeToolCall (lines 548-620), with ToolCall kind: shell_command/powershell -> .command, title `ToolTitles.unwrapShell(command)` or "Shell command", detail = `description`, plus "in the background" joined with " · " when `run_in_background == true`; monitor_command -> .command, command or "Monitor command"; shell_output -> .command "Shell output" (detail id ?? task_id); shell_tasks -> .command "Shell tasks"; kill_shell -> .command "Stop shell" (detail id ?? task_id ?? pid); read_file -> .read, title `path("file_path") ?? path("path") ?? "Read file"` (relative path, falling back from key `file_path` to key `path`), detail "lines <offset>–<offset+limit>" (en dash) when both ints present; read_directory -> .search, path("path") or "List files"; write_file -> .edit, path("file_path") or "Write file" (no `path` fallback) with FileEdit(path, old: snapshot ?? "", new: content); edit_file -> .edit, title `path("file_path") ?? path("path") ?? "Edit file"`, FileEdit path also `path("file_path") ?? path("path")`, old = old_string ?? old_text ?? old ?? "", new = new_string ?? new_text ?? new ?? ""; glob -> .search, pattern or "Find files", detail path; grep -> .search, pattern or "Search", detail path and glob joined by " · " (nil when empty); web_fetch -> .web, url or "Fetch page"; web_search -> .web, query or "Search the web"; agent -> .agent, description ?? singleLine(prompt, limit 96) ?? "Sub-agent", detail subagent_type; agent_output -> .agent "Agent output" detail agent_id; activate_skill -> .other "Skill · <name or empty>"; enter_worktree/exit_worktree -> .other, humanized name, detail name; run_command -> .other "Command · <command ?? name ?? empty>"; names with prefix `mcp__` -> .mcp: `parts = name.split(separator: "__", omittingEmptySubsequences: true)`, server = `parts.count > 1 ? String(parts[1]) : "MCP"`, tool = `parts.count > 2 ? parts[2...].joined(separator: "__") : name` (the whole name), title "<server> · <tool>", detail `input.isNull ? nil : input.compactString` with NO 300-char limit and NO "{}" filter; any other name -> .other, humanized name ("Task create" from task_create) with compactString detail only if non-empty, not "{}" and count <= 300.

Subagent progress (lines 394-399): requires `toolCallId` and `toolName`; subject taken from `event["toolInput"]` keys command ?? file_path ?? pattern ?? query ?? url; line = `subject.map { "\(tool)  \(TextCleanup.singleLine($0, limit: 100))" } ?? tool` (two spaces), so with no subject the line is just the tool name; emitted as `.toolOutput(id:, text: line + "\n")`.

Notices: compaction_start -> info "Compacting context."; compaction_done reads `event["tokensSaved"]?.int ?? 0` (line 405) and, when > 0, shows "Compacted context, freeing \(saved.formatted()) tokens." where `Int.formatted()` groups digits by the current locale (e.g. "12,345" in en_US), else "Compacted context."; warning "Command Code stopped at its cap of 400 round trips for one message. Send another to carry on."
No views, geometry, colours or animations in this file.
feature_notes: start(): no executable -> ProviderError.notInstalled(configuration.provider); a resume id with no transcript in any `~/.commandcode/projects/*/<id>.jsonl` throws ProviderError.failed("Command Code no longer has this conversation; starting a new one."); returns sessionID or "".

send(): not running -> ProviderError.notRunning; turn active -> ProviderError.failed("Command Code is still on the last turn."). Updates runtimeMode, interactionMode, model (only when input.model non-empty), effort (always overwritten), isFinalReport; `turnCounter += 1`; then resets exactly `turnActive = true`, `interruptRequested = false`, `runResult = nil`, `runError = nil`, `streamedText = false`, and `removeAll()` on editSnapshots, toolNames and toolInputs (lines 134-142). It does NOT reset messageCounter, thinkingCounter, messageText, thinkingText or activeModel, so `cc-<launchID>-m<n>` / `-r<n>` counters keep rising across turns for the life of the session (currentMessageID/currentThinkingID are cleared in didClose, lines 438-439).

Argument order: -p, --output-format json, --skip-onboarding, --no-auto-update, --trust, --tools-enable todo_write, --max-turns (1 when isFinalReport else 400), then --model <model>, --effort <effort> only when CommandCodeAPI.efforts(for: model) contains it, then `--permission-mode plan` in plan mode else `--yolo`, then `--mod <modURL.path>` when runtimeMode != .fullAccess OR plan mode OR MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL exists, then `--resume <sessionID>`.

Spawn failure: turnActive = false and ProviderError.failed("Command Code could not start: <localizedDescription>"). After start: stdin gets the prompt, input closed, then .turnStarted(providerTurnID: nil). Read task handles each message, then awaits waitForExit and calls didClose.

prompt: input.text plus, for images whose path exists, "

Attached files (read them with read_file):
" and "- <path>" lines joined by newline.
interrupt(): only when turnActive; sets interruptRequested and terminates. compact() always throws "Command Code compacts its context on its own." answerQuestion is a no-op.
resolveApproval: unknown id ignored; "allow"/"always" reply allow ("always" also inserts grantKey(kind) into sessionGrants); anything else denies; then .requestResolved(id:).
stop(): stopped = true, turnActive = false, terminate, stop watcher, remove approval directory.
handle(): type "event" -> handleEvent(message.event); type "result" -> RunResult(subtype default "success", stopReason, errorText(error)) and sessionId adoption with .sessionReady when new.

Events: run_start adopts sessionId; message_start: messageCounter += 1, id "cc-<launchID>-m<n>", messageText = "", streamedText = false; text_delta: returns on missing or empty `delta`, creates `cc-<launchID>-m<n>` (incrementing messageCounter) when currentMessageID is nil, sets streamedText, appends and streams .messageDelta; thinking_start: thinkingCounter += 1, id "cc-<launchID>-r<n>", thinkingText = ""; thinking_delta (lines 311-318): likewise returns on missing or empty `delta`, and `if currentThinkingID == nil { thinkingCounter += 1; currentThinkingID = "cc-\(launchID)-r\(thinkingCounter)" }`, then appends to thinkingText and streams .reasoningDelta; thinking_end emits .reasoningCompleted with event `text` or buffer when non-blank, then clears currentThinkingID; message_end emits .messageCompleted with streamed text (or content text if buffer empty) when streamed, else content text when non-blank, then clears both current ids; model_request_start/end set activeModel; model_request_end usage inputTokens+outputTokens > 0 -> .usage(ContextUsage(usedTokens, windowTokens: contextWindow(activeModel ?? model))), TokenLedger record, .tokenSpend(provider .commandcode, total, input, output, model: activeModel).

tool_queued: records name/input; todo_write -> .todos only; write_file snapshots file_path ("" when unreadable); .toolStarted then scanApprovals(). tool_update -> .toolUpdated output from partial when non-empty. tool_completed -> status .completed, output from result, edits = finishEdit. tool_errored -> output errorText or "The tool failed.", status .failed, edits finishEdit. tool_hook_blocked/tool_denied -> output hookOutput or denyMessage or "Declined.", status .declined, snapshot dropped, pending approval resolved. todo_write ids are skipped for update/complete/error/deny.

subagent_progress -> .toolOutput line; session_titled -> .title when non-empty; compaction_start/done notices; notice -> level error/.error, warning or warn/.warning, else .info; run_error stores errorText; interrupted sets interruptRequested; run_end in plan mode with non-blank result.finalText -> .planCompleted(id: "cc-<launchID>-plan<turnCounter>", markdown). Ignored: turn_start, turn_end, message_update, model_trace, tool_running, tool_hooks, tool_input_repaired, subagent_start, subagent_stop.

didClose: ignores a stale process; clears turn state, resolves every pending approval, clears approval files; if stopped returns silently. interruptRequested or status 130 -> .turnCompleted(status: .interrupted, error: nil), checked before any result line. With a result line: subtype "success" -> completed (cap notice when stopReason "max_turns"); "max_turns" -> cap notice + completed; other -> error = result.error ?? runError ?? lastLines(errorTail) ?? "Command Code stopped before finishing.", .usageLimit(resetsAt: nil) when isRateLimit, then .failed with friendlyError(error).

Exit codes without a result line: 0 completed; 3 "Command Code is not signed in. Run `cmd login` in Terminal, or add a Studio API key in Settings → Providers → Command Code."; 4 tail or "Command Code was denied permission."; 5 .usageLimit then tail or "Command Code is rate limited. Wait for the window to reset, or buy on-demand credits, which are never throttled."; 6 "Could not reach Command Code. Check the connection and try again."; 7 tail or "Command Code's API returned a server error. Try again in a moment."; 8 cap notice + completed; 9 "The model produced no response."; 10 "Command Code is out of credits. Top up at commandcode.ai/billing, or wait for the monthly credits to reset."; default runError ?? tail ?? "Command Code exited with code <status>."

noteTurnCap is suppressed when isFinalReport. isRateLimit: lowercased contains "rate limit", "usage exceeded" or "window limit". friendlyError: "not authenticated"/"unauthorized"/"session expired" -> the not-signed-in text; "insufficient credits"/"out of credits" -> the out-of-credits text; else unchanged.
errorText: null -> nil; string (empty -> nil); object `message`; else compactString unless "{}". text(in:): string as is, or array blocks' `text`, image blocks "[image]", joined by "\n".
todos: input.todos items, text from content/text/title; status completed/done -> .done, in_progress/active -> .active, else .pending.

finishEdit: only for ids with a snapshot and a file_path input; after = current file snapshot or ""; unchanged -> [FileEdit(path: relative)], else old/new pair. snapshot(): nil when size unknown or > 1_000_000 or not UTF-8.

scanApprovals: requires approvalDirectory and turnActive; files sorted by name, only `.request.json`; unparsable skipped (not deleted); parsed file deleted; id from toolCallId else file name minus suffix; duplicates skipped; decide().
decide: autoApproves or sessionGrants contains grantKey(kind) -> reply allow silently; else store pending and emit .approval.

autoApproves: .fullAccess true; .supervised false; .autoAcceptEdits only write_file/edit_file; .auto edits true, shell_command/powershell/monitor_command true when !ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles(command), kill_shell/cron_create/cron_delete/task_stop true, otherwise false.

makeApproval kind (lines 719-725): `switch call.kind { case .command: .command; case .edit: .fileChange; default: .tool }`, where call = makeToolCall(name:input:snapshot:). ToolCall kinds per tool: shell_command, powershell, monitor_command, shell_output, shell_tasks, kill_shell -> .command; read_file -> .read; read_directory, glob, grep -> .search; write_file, edit_file -> .edit; web_fetch, web_search -> .web; agent, agent_output -> .agent; activate_skill, enter_worktree, exit_worktree, run_command and any unlisted name -> .other; `mcp__*` -> .mcp. So approval kinds are: command for those six, fileChange for write_file/edit_file, tool for everything else. grantKey: .command "command", .fileChange "fileChange", .tool/.permissions/.plan "tool". One "Approve for session" therefore covers e.g. kill_shell and monitor_command together with shell_command ("command"), and every mcp__ tool together with any other non-command, non-edit call ("tool"). Note that the mod's READ_ONLY set (CommandCodeAPI.swift:377-383) never sends read_file, read_directory, glob, grep, shell_output, shell_tasks, web_search, web_fetch, agent, agent_output, activate_skill or run_command to the gate, so in practice the "tool" grant is shared by mcp__ tools, enter_worktree/exit_worktree and unlisted tools such as cron_create or task_stop.

B1->B2: three mechanical refactors only, each `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` replaced by the B2 helper `.trimmed` (Text.swift:132, same definition): line 322 in thinking_end (`!text.trimmed.isEmpty`), line 331 in message_end (`!text.trimmed.isEmpty`), and line 423 in run_end (`interactionMode == .plan, !finalText.trimmed.isEmpty`). Behaviour unchanged (3 insertions, 3 deletions).
